reveal.subject: Great Barrier Reef

sources.excerpt: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands stretching for over 2,300 kilometres (1,400 mi) over an area of approximately 344,400 square kilometres (133,000 mi2).
The reef is located in the Coral Sea, off the coast of Queensland, Australia. It is separated from the coast by a channel 160 kilometres (100 mi) wide in places and over 61 metres (200 ft) deep.

The Great Barrier Reef can be seen from outer space and is the world's biggest single structure made by living organisms. This reef structure is composed of and built by billions of tiny organisms, known as coral polyps. It supports a wide diversity of life and was selected as a World Heritage Site in 1981.
A large part of the reef is protected by the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, which helps to limit the impact of human use, such as fishing and tourism.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: the Belize Barrier Reef and the New Caledonia barrier reef are large but far smaller; the Ningaloo Reef is on the other side of Australia and is a fringing reef; the Coral Sea is where this one sits, not the answer. No alias is offered because the name is always given in full.
